properties.name: Missing Signer Check
properties.invariant_template: Every privileged instruction MUST validate that the expected signer account has actually signed the transaction.
properties.description: An instruction handler fails to verify that a required account has signed the transaction, allowing any user to invoke privileged operations (e.g. admin withdrawals, parameter changes) without authorization.
properties.remediation: Use Anchor's `Signer<'info>` type or `#[account(signer)]` constraint for every authority account.

properties.name: Account Ownership Validation
properties.invariant_template: Every deserialized account MUST be validated to be owned by the expected program before use.
properties.description: An instruction accepts an account without verifying its owner program, allowing an attacker to pass a fake account owned by a different program with crafted data.

annotations.common_vuln: Using unchecked `AccountInfo` instead of typed `Account<'info, T>`

properties.remediation: Use Anchor typed accounts (`Account<'info, T>`) which automatically validate ownership and deserialization.

properties.name: PDA & Bump Validation
properties.invariant_template: Every PDA account MUST be derived with the correct seeds and its bump seed MUST be validated (stored or canonical).
properties.description: A Program Derived Address is accepted without verifying its derivation seeds or bump, allowing an attacker to supply a different PDA or a non-canonical bump to access/modify unintended state.
properties.remediation: Always use `#[account(seeds = [..], bump)]` constraints and store the canonical bump on initialization.

properties.name: Duplicate Account Aliasing
properties.invariant_template: When an instruction takes multiple accounts of the same type, each account MUST be proven distinct (no aliasing).
properties.description: An instruction handler accepts two accounts (e.g. `from` and `to`) without checking they are distinct. An attacker passes the same account for both, potentially doubling balances or bypassing transfer checks.

annotations.common_vuln: No key equality check between same-type accounts

properties.remediation: Add explicit `constraint = a.key() != b.key()` for every pair of same-type accounts.

properties.name: CPI Program-ID Validation
properties.invariant_template: Every Cross-Program Invocation MUST validate the target program's ID before invoking it.
properties.description: A CPI call is made using a program account passed by the user without verifying its program ID, allowing an attacker to redirect the CPI to a malicious program.

annotations.common_vuln: Using unchecked AccountInfo for CPI target program

properties.remediation: Use Anchor's `Program<'info, T>` type for CPI target programs, or explicitly check `program.key() == expected_program_id`.

properties.name: Sysvar Account Validation
properties.invariant_template: Sysvar accounts (Clock, Rent, etc.) MUST be validated against their known addresses or accessed via sysvar API.
properties.description: A sysvar account (Rent, Clock, etc.) is accepted as a user-supplied AccountInfo without verifying it matches the canonical sysvar address, allowing data spoofing.
properties.remediation: Use Anchor's `Sysvar<'info, T>` type or `Clock::get()` / `Rent::get()` sysvar API.

properties.name: Arithmetic Overflow
properties.invariant_template: All arithmetic operations on token amounts and balances MUST use checked/saturating math to prevent overflow/underflow.
properties.description: Arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication) on u64 balances or amounts are performed without overflow checks, potentially wrapping around and creating or destroying value.
properties.remediation: Replace all `+`, `-`, `*` on financial values with `checked_add()`, `checked_sub()`, `checked_mul()` and handle the `None` case with a custom error.

properties.name: Signer & Authority Mismatch
properties.invariant_template: The signer of a privileged instruction MUST match the authority stored in the target account's state.
properties.description: An instruction checks that *some* account signed the transaction but does not verify that the signer matches the authority/owner stored in the account being modified.

annotations.common_vuln: Signer present but not matched against stored authority pubkey

properties.remediation: Use `#[account(has_one = authority)]` or explicitly compare `signer.key() == account.authority`.

properties.name: State Transition Invariant
properties.invariant_template: Account state transitions MUST follow a valid finite-state machine — illegal transitions MUST be rejected.
properties.description: An instruction modifies account state without validating the current state, allowing invalid transitions (e.g. finalizing an already-finalized auction, withdrawing from an uninitialized vault).

annotations.common_vuln: Missing state enum check before mutation

properties.remediation: Define an explicit state enum and validate the current state before every mutation with a `require!()` or `match` guard.

properties.name: CPI Cross-Instruction Assumptions
properties.invariant_template: A CPI caller MUST NOT assume the callee's return data or state effects without post-CPI validation.
properties.description: After a CPI call, the calling program assumes success or specific state changes without checking the return data or re-reading the modified accounts, leaving the program vulnerable to a callee that fails silently or returns unexpected data.

annotations.common_vuln: No post-CPI account reload or return data check
annotations.pattern: invoke() followed by immediate state mutation without reload

properties.remediation: After every CPI, reload affected accounts and validate expected post-conditions before continuing.
